paragraphs: Throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K and the notes to consolidated financial statements, references to "Hamilton Beach Holding", "the Company", "we", "us" and "our" and similar references are to Hamilton Beach Brands Holding Company and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis unless otherwise noted or as the context otherwise requires. Hamilton Beach Brands Holding Company is a holding company and operates through its indirect, wholly owned subsidiary, Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("HBB").

We are a leading designer, marketer and distributor of a wide range of brand name small electric household and specialty housewares appliances, and commercial products for restaurants, fast food chains, bars and hotels, and a provider of connected devices and software for home healthcare management.

Our operations are managed and reported in two operating segments, each of which is a reportable segment for financial reporting purposes: (1) Home and Commercial Products and (2) Health. During the year ended December 31, 2023, the Company had one operating and one reportable segment.

Our Home and Commercial Products segment includes consumer product revenue, primarily concentrated in North America, consisting of sales of small electric household and specialty housewares appliances to traditional brick and mortar and ecommerce retailers, distributors and directly to the end consumer. Also included in this segment is commercial product revenue consisting of sales of products for restaurants, fast-food chains, bars and hotels. Approximately two-thirds of the Company's commercial sales are in the United States ("U.S.") and the remaining is in markets across the globe.

Our Health segment includes lease revenue in the U.S. and globally associated with leases of connected devices to specialty pharmacy networks and pharmaceutical companies, as well as licensing revenue associated with agreements which grant customers the right to use software for healthcare management.

We make our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and any amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") available, free of charge, through our website, www.hamiltonbeachbrands.com, as soon as reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with, or furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). The content of our website is not incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K or in any other report or document we file with the SEC, and any references to our website is intended to be inactive textual references only.

We design, market and distribute a wide range of brand name small electric household and specialty housewares appliances, including air fryers, blenders, coffee makers, food processors, indoor electric grills, irons, juicers, mixers, slow cookers, toasters and toaster ovens. We also design, market and distribute commercial products for restaurants, fast food chains, bars and hotels. We generally market our "good" and "better" consumer products under the Hamilton Beach®, Proctor Silex®,and Weston® brands. We participate in the consumer premium market with our owned brands Hamilton Beach® Professional and Lotus® and license the brands for CHI® premium garment care products and Clorox™ home appliances. The Lotus® brand launched in September 2025 and offers high-end, premium small kitchen appliances. We market our commercial products under the Hamilton Beach Commercial® and the Proctor Silex Commercial® brands and we have multi-year license agreements to design, sell and distribute Sunkist® commercial juicers and sectionizers and Numilk® plant-based milk makers. We also license certain of our trademarks to various licensees in categories such as microwave ovens, among others. We continue to expand in the home, health and wellness markets. In February 2024, the Company acquired HealthBeacon Limited ("HealthBeacon") a medical technology firm and strategic partner of the Company. HealthBeacon develops digitally connected devices that enable patients to manage at home chronic conditions that require the use of injectable medications, and it provides other health services. The primary system offered is the Smart Sharps Bin™ from Hamilton Beach Health®.

Sales from our Home and Commercial Products segment are generated predominantly by a network of inside sales employees to mass merchandisers, ecommerce retailers, department stores, warehouse clubs, specialty home retailers, distributors, restaurants, bars, hotels and other retail outlets. Sales from our Health segment are generated through specialty pharmacy and pharmaceutical companies.

Walmart Inc. and its global subsidiaries ("Walmart") accounted for approximately 29%, 29% and 27% of our revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. Amazon.com, Inc. and its subsidiaries ("Amazon.com") accounted for approximately 19%, 24% and 24% of our revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. Our five largest customers accounted for approximately 62%, 65% and 64% of our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Our warranty program to the consumer consists generally of an assurance-type limited warranty lasting for varying periods of up to ten years for electric appliances, with the majority of products having a warranty of one to three years. There is no guarantee to the consumer as we may repair or replace, at our option, those products returned under warranty.

The market for small electric household and specialty housewares appliances is fairly steady throughout the year, however our revenue typically increases during the second half of the year and peaks during the fourth quarter due to the fall holiday-selling season. We generally use cash on hand or borrowings under our $125 million senior secured floating-rate revolving credit facility (the "HBB Facility") to finance inventory over the course of the year in anticipation of the fall holiday-selling season.

We hold patents and trademarks registered in the U.S. and foreign countries for various products. We believe that our business is not dependent upon any individual patent, copyright or license, but that the Hamilton Beach® trademark is material to our business.
We incurred $13.2 million, $13.7 million and $12.4 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, in expenses on product design and development activities.

Our products are produced to our specifications by third-party suppliers. We do not maintain long-term purchase contracts with suppliers and operate mainly on a purchase order basis. We negotiate the purchases from our foreign suppliers in U.S. dollars.

headings: Industry Risks
Our business is sensitive to the strength of the North American consumer markets and weakness in these markets could adversely affect our business.
The concentration of our brand name small electric household and specialty housewares appliance sales among a few retailers could materially reduce revenue and profitability.
Our inability to compete effectively with competitors in our industry could result in lost market share and decreased revenue.
Changes in consumer shopping trends and changes in distribution channels could result in lost market share and decreased revenue and profitability.
The markets for our products are dependent on consumer spending and typically peak in the fourth quarter, which could result in significant variations in revenue and profitability.
Business Risks
Increases in costs of products may materially reduce our profitability.
Substantial disruptions at any of our distribution centers could have an adverse effect on our business, operating results and financial condition.
Certain products rely upon a single third-party supplier.
We are subject to changes in our customers' inventory management strategies.

Our expansion into the health and wellness market may result in unexpected challenges and inefficiencies, which could have an adverse effect on our business, operating results and financial condition.
Our ability to attract, retain and develop key talent is crucial to our results of operations and future growth.
Our business could suffer if information technology systems are disrupted, cease to operate effectively or become subject to a cybersecurity incident.
Failure to comply with personal data protection and privacy laws could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
The Company's good reputation is critical to the success of our business.
Financial Risks
Our financing arrangements contain various restrictions that could limit operating flexibility.
We are subject to foreign currency exchange risk.
Regulatory Risks
We may become subject to claims under foreign laws and regulations, which may be expensive, time-consuming and distracting.
Our obligations relating to environmental matters may exceed our expectations.
The Company is subject to litigation risk which could adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and liquidity.
Our intellectual property rights could be infringed and adverse events regarding licensed intellectual property could harm our business.
Our business subjects us to product liability claims, which could affect our reputation, revenue and profitability.
Our business involves the potential for product recalls, which could affect our revenue and profitability.
Failure to comply with public health, consumer protection and other regulations could affect our reputation, revenue and profitability.
Compliance with multiple, and potentially conflicting, domestic and international laws and regulations, including anti-corruption laws, may be difficult, burdensome or expensive.
Government regulations could impose costly requirements on our business.

Changes in U.S. and foreign trade policies, tariffs and other government actions may increase our costs, disrupt our supply chain or otherwise adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Risks Related to Our Common Stock
The amount and frequency of dividend payments made on the Company's common stock could change.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to various risks and uncertainties. Any of the risks and uncertainties described below could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations and should be considered in evaluating us. Although the risks are organized by headings and each risk is described separately, many of the risks are interrelated. While we believe we have identified and discussed below the key risk factors affecting our business, there may be additional risks and uncertainties that are not presently known or that are not currently believed to be significant that may adversely affect our business, performance or financial condition in the future.

The strength of the economy in the U.S., and to a lesser degree in Canada and Mexico, has a significant impact on our performance. Weakness in consumer confidence and poor financial performance by mass merchandisers, ecommerce retailers, warehouse clubs, department stores or any of our other customers could result in reduced revenue and profitability. A general slowdown in the consumer sector could result in additional pricing and marketing support pressures on the Company. Additionally, in periods of uncertain economic conditions, such as tariffs, inflation, rising interest rates, recessions or economic slowdowns, our customers may purchase less of our products as they manage their inventory levels to adjust to changes in consumers' spending habits in response to such economic conditions. These circumstances could adversely impact our revenue and profitability.

Our business is dependent on key customers and the loss of, or significant decline in business from, one or more of our key customers could materially reduce our revenue and profitability and our ability to sustain or grow our business.

We rely on several key customers in our consumer business. During fiscal 2025, Walmart and Amazon.com accounted for approximately 29% and 19% of our revenue, respectively. Although we have long-established relationships with many customers, including Walmart and Amazon.com, we do not have any long-term supply contracts with these customers, and purchases are generally made using individual purchase orders. A loss of or significant reduction in sales to any key customer could result in significant decreases in our revenue and profitability and an inability to sustain or grow our business.

We must receive a continuous flow of new orders from our large, high-volume retail customers. Failure to obtain anticipated orders or delays or cancellations of orders or significant pressure to reduce prices from key customers could impair our ability to sustain or grow our business. In addition, we may be unable to continually meet the needs of those customers, which could damage our customer relationships and result in reduced new orders.

Management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our historical financial statements and related notes thereto and the other disclosures contained elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The following discussion and analysis focuses on our financial results for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 and year-to-year comparisons between these years. A discussion of our results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 is included in Part II, Item 7 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.
CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES

Our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based upon our consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP). The preparation of financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities (if any). Actual results could differ from those estimates.
We believe the following critical accounting policies affect our more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of our consolidated financial statements.

Revenue Recognition: Revenue is recognized when control of the promised goods or services is transferred to our customers, in an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to be entitled to in exchange for those goods or services. Sales taxes are excluded from revenue. At contract inception, we assess the goods and services promised in our contracts with customers and identify a performance obligation for each promised good or service that is distinct. We have elected to account for shipping and handling activities performed after a customer obtains control of the goods as activities to fulfill the promise to transfer the goods, and therefore these activities are not assessed as a separate service to customers. The amount of revenue recognized varies primarily with price concessions and changes in returns. We offer price concessions to our customers for incentive offerings, special pricing agreements, price competition, promotions or other volume-based arrangements. We determine whether price concessions offered to our customers are a reduction of the transaction price and revenue or are advertising expense, depending on whether we receive a distinct good or service from our customers and, if so, whether we can reasonably estimate the fair value of that distinct good or service. We evaluated such agreements with our customers and determined they should be accounted for as variable consideration.

To estimate variable consideration, we apply both the expected value method and most likely amount method based on the form of variable consideration, according to which method would provide the better prediction. The expected value method involves a probability weighted determination of the expected amount, whereas the most likely amount method identifies the single most likely outcome in a range of possible amounts.

We monitor our estimates of variable consideration, which includes returns and price concessions, and periodically adjust the carrying amounts as appropriate. During 2025, there were no material adjustments to the aforesaid estimates, and our past results of operations have not been materially affected by a change in these estimates. Although there can be no assurances, we are not aware of any circumstances that would be reasonably likely to materially change these estimates in the future.

Deferred Taxes: We determine deferred tax assets and/or liabilities by multiplying the differences between the financial reporting and tax reporting bases for assets and liabilities by the enacted tax rates expected to be in effect when such differences are recovered or settled if there is no change in law. The effect on deferred taxes of a change in tax rates is recognized in net income in the period that includes the enactment date. Valuation allowances on deferred tax assets are estimated based on our assessment of the realizability of such amounts.

paragraphs: 本年度報告表10-K及財務會計彙編說明書之附註中，提及「Hamilton Beach Holding」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」等詞彙，均指Hamilton Beach Brands Holding Company及其子公司於合併基礎上，除非另有說明或根據上下文另有要求。Hamilton Beach Brands Holding Company為一控股公司，透過其間接、完全擁有之子公司Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc.（位於德國特拉華州之公司，簡稱HBB）進行營運。
我們為一領導品牌之設計、行銷與分銷者，產品範圍包含各式小型電動家用及專業居家用電器，以及供餐廳、速食連鎖店、酒吧與旅館使用之商業產品，同時亦為居家醫療管理之連線裝置與軟體之供應商。
我們之營運分為兩大營運分部，每一營運分部於財務報導上均為應報告分部：(1)居家與商業產品，(2)健康。於2023年12月31日為止之會計年度，本公司有一營運分部與一應報告分部。
居家與商業產品分部包含消費者產品之營收，主要集中於北美地區，包含向傳統實體零售商店、電商零售商、經銷商及直接向終端消費者銷售之小型電動家用及專業居家用電器。此分部亦包含商業產品之營收，包含向餐廳、速食連鎖店、酒吧與旅館銷售之產品。本公司約兩-thirds之商業銷售為美國（"U.S.")，其餘則為全球各地之市場。
我們的健康應報告分部包含美國與全球的租賃收入，與連線裝置租賃給專門藥房網路及藥品公司有關，以及與授予客戶使用軟體進行醫療管理權利的契約相關的授權收入。

我們依照 Form 10-K 進行年度報告，依照 Form 10-Q 進行季度報告，依照 Form 8-K 進行現況報告，以及任何對這些報告的更正或補充，並依照 1934 年證券交易法第 13(a) 或 15(d) 節的規定，向證券交易委員會（"SEC"）提交或提供後，免費提供於我們的網站 www.hamiltonbeachbrands.com，儘可能在資料電子提交或提供後立即提供。我們網站的內容未經引用納入本年度 Form 10-K 報告，或任何其他我們向 SEC 提交的報告或文件，且任何提及我們網站的參考僅為無效文字參考。

我們設計、行銷與分銷廣泛的知名品牌的家用小型電器與專業廚房用具，包括空氣炸鍋、攪拌機、咖啡機、食物處理機、室內電氣烤架、熨斗、果汁機、攪拌器、慢燉鍋、吐司機與吐司烤箱。我們也設計、行銷與分銷餐廳、速食連鎖店、酒吧與飯店用的商用產品。我們通常以 Hamilton Beach®、Proctor Silex® 和 Weston® 品牌行銷我們的 "好" 與 "更好" 消費者產品。我們透過自有品牌 Hamilton Beach® Professional 和 Lotus® 參與消費者高階市場，並授權 CHI® 高階衣物護理產品與 Clorox™ 家用電器品牌。Lotus® 品牌於 2025 年 9 月推出，提供高階、高品質的小型廚房電器。我們以 Hamilton Beach Commercial® 和 Proctor Silex Commercial® 品牌行銷我們的商用產品，我們擁有多年授權契約，設計、銷售與分銷 Sunkist® 商用果汁機與切片機以及 Numilk® 植基乳製造機。我們也授權部分自有商標給其他類別的授權商，例如微波爐等。我們持續擴展在居家、健康與 wellness 市場。2024 年 2 月，本公司取得 HealthBeacon Limited（"HealthBeacon"）這家醫療科技公司（本公司戰略夥伴）。HealthBeacon 開發可讓患者在家管理需使用注射藥物的慢性病狀的數位連線裝置，並提供其他健康服務。主要提供的系統為 Hamilton Beach Health® 的 Smart Sharps Bin™。
我們居家與商用產品應報告分部的銷售主要由內部銷售人員網路產生，銷售對象為通路商、電商零售商、百貨公司、倉儲俱樂部、專業居家零售商、經銷商、餐廳、酒吧、飯店及其他零售通路。我們健康應報告分部的銷售則透過專門藥房與藥品公司產生。

Walmart Inc. 以及其全球子公司（"Walmart"）在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別佔本公司營業收入約 29%、29% 及 27%。Amazon.com, Inc. 以及其子公司（"Amazon.com"）在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別佔本公司營業收入約 19%、24% 及 24%。本公司前五大客戶在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別佔本公司營業收入約 62%、65% 及 64%。
我們對消費者提供的保固方案，通常為一種保證型有限保固，保固期間為電器產品不等於十年，大多數產品的保固期間為一至三年。我們對消費者無任何保證，我們可選擇修復或更換在保固期間內退回的產品。
小型電動家用及專用廚房用具市場全年大致穩定，然而我們的營業收入通常在年中後段增加，並在第四季達到高峯，這是因應秋季節日購物季的影響。我們通常會利用現金或透過我們的 125 百萬美元高級抵押浮動利率週轉信用融資 (the "HBB Facility") 借款來支應全年存貨，以預備秋季節日購物季的銷售。
本公司持有在美國及海外國家註冊的專利及商標，用於各種產品。我們認為本公司業務並非依賴任何單一專利、著作權或授權，但 Hamilton Beach® 商標對本公司業務而言屬重要。
本公司在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別產生 $13.2 百萬、$13.7 百萬及 $12.4 百萬的費用，用於產品設計及開發活動。
本公司產品由第三方供應商根據本公司規格製造。本公司與供應商並無長期採購合約，主要採用訂單採購方式進行營運。我們與海外供應商的採購交易以美元結算。

管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析應與我們的歷史財務報表及其相關附註，以及本年度10-K表報中其他揭露資訊一併閱讀。以下討論與分析重點說明我們2025年12月31日財年與2024年12月31日財年之財務結果，以及這兩年間的年對年比較。有關2024年12月31日財年與2023年12月31日財年營運結果之比較說明，請參閱我們2024年12月31日財年10-K表報之第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」。
關鍵會計政策與會計估計
我們對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析係基於我們合併財務報表，該財務報表係依照美國通用會計準則（GAAP）編製。財務報表之編製需要管理層做出會計估計與假設，這些估計與假設會影響所報導之資產、負債、收入、費用及揭露之或有資產與負債（如有）。實際結果可能與這些估計不同。
我們認為以下關鍵會計政策會影響我們在編製合併財務報表時所使用之較重要判斷與估計。

收入認列：收入於本公司承諾之商品或服務之控制權轉移至客戶時認列，認列金額反映本公司預期可就這些商品或服務所獲得之對價。銷售稅不包含於收入中。於合約開始時，我們評估與客戶合約中承諾之商品或服務，並為每一項獨立之承諾商品或服務識別一項履行義務。我們已選擇將客戶取得商品控制權後所進行之運送與處理活動視為履行轉移商品之承諾活動，因此這些活動不被視為對客戶之獨立服務。收入認列之金額主要取決於價格讓利與退貨之變動。我們為客戶提供價格讓利，作為激勵方案、特殊價格協議、價格競爭、促銷或其他基於交易量之安排。我們判斷為客戶提供之價格讓利係為交易價格與收入之減項，或為廣告費用，視我們是否從客戶處取得獨立之商品或服務，以及如取得，是否能合理估算該獨立商品或服務之公允價值而定。我們評估與客戶之相關協議，並決定應將其視為變動對價處理。
為估算變動對價，我們根據變動對價之形式，應用期望值法與最可能金額法中之較佳預測方法。期望值法涉及根據機率加權確定預期金額，而最可能金額法則識別可能金額範圍中之單一最可能結果。
我們監測變動對價之估計，包括退貨與價格讓利，並在適當時機調整其帳面價值。2025年期間，對上述估計未有重大調整，且過去營運結果未因這些估計之變動而受到重大影響。雖然無法保證，但我們未知悉任何可能合理導致這些估計在未來重大變動之情況。
遞延稅項：我們透過將資產與負債的財務報導基準與稅務報導基準之間的差異乘以預期在該差異被償還或結清時生效的已訂稅率，來計算遞延稅資產與/或負債。稅率變動對遞延稅項的影響，在包含立法生效日的會計期間內，會計入淨收入。遞延稅資產的價值減損準備，係根據我們對該金額可實現性的評估來進行估計。

我們的營運成果如下，為截至12月31日之各年度：
營業收入 - 總營業收入較前一年減少 47.8 百萬美元，或 7.3%，這是因為本公司美國消費業務在第二及第三季的銷售量較低，零售商為評估存貨水準與美國新課徵關稅所導致的價格上漲而暫停採購。此下降幅度部分被商用與健康業務的營收成長所抵銷。

headings: 產業風險
本公司業務對北美消費者市場的強弱程度相當敏感，若這些市場表現不佳，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司品牌名稱的小型電動家用及專用居家器具電器銷售集中於少數零售商，這可能會顯著降低營業收入與獲利能力。
本公司若無法在產業中有效競爭，可能會導致市佔率流失與營收減少。
消費者購物趨勢的變化及銷售通路的變動，可能會導致市佔率流失與營收及獲利能力下降。
本公司產品的市場依賴消費者支出，通常在第四季達到高峯，這可能會導致營收與獲利能力出現顯著波動。
業務風險
產品成本的增加可能會顯著降低本公司的獲利能力。
本公司任一配送中心發生重大幹擾，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
部分產品依賴單一第三方供應商。
本公司受客戶存貨管理策略變動之影響。
本公司擴張至健康與 wellness 市場，可能導致未預見之挑戰與低效率，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司吸引、留住並培養關鍵人才之能力，對本公司營運成果及未來成長至關重要。
若資訊科技系統受幹擾、無法有效運作或遭遇網路安全事件，本公司業務可能受影響。
未能遵守個人資料保護及隱私權法規，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司良好聲譽對本公司業務成功至關重要。
財務風險
本公司之融資安排包含多項限制，可能限制營運彈性。
本公司受外幣匯率風險影響。
法規風險
本公司可能因涉外法規而面臨聲請，此等聲請可能耗費金錢、時間且分散管理注意力。
本公司有關環境事項之義務可能高於預期。
本公司受訴訟風險影響，可能不利於財務狀況、營運成果與流動性。
本公司之智慧財產權可能遭侵害，且有關授權智慧財產權之不利事件可能影響本公司業務。
本公司業務面臨產品責任爭議之風險，可能影響本公司聲譽、營業收入及獲利能力。
本公司業務涉及產品回收之潛在風險，可能影響本公司營業收入及獲利能力。
未能遵守公共衛生、消費者保護及其他規範，可能影響本公司聲譽、營業收入及獲利能力。
遵守多項且可能相互衝突之國內外法律及規範，包括反貪污法律，可能困難、負擔沉重或成本高昂。
政府規範可能對本公司業務課以高昂之要求。
美國及外國貿易政策、關稅及其他政府措施之變動，可能提高本公司成本、幹擾本公司供應鏈或以其他方式不利影響本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果。
與本公司普通股相關之風險
本公司普通股所發放之股息金額及發放頻率可能變動。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨多種風險與不確定性。下列所描述的任何風險與不確定性，均可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響，評估本公司時應予以考量。雖然風險已按標題分類，且每項風險均分別說明，但許多風險彼此相關。儘管本公司認為已識別並討論了影響本公司業務的主要風險因素，但未來仍可能有其他未預見或目前認為不具重大影響的風險與不確定性，可能對本公司業務、營運表現或財務狀況造成不利影響。

美國經濟的強弱，以及較小程度的加拿大與墨西哥經濟，對本公司營運表現有重大影響。消費者信心不足，或大型百貨商、電商零售商、倉儲俱樂部、連鎖百貨公司或其他客戶的財務表現不佳，可能會導致營收與獲利減少。整體消費領域的放緩，可能使本公司面臨更高的價格與行銷支援壓力。此外，在經濟不確定時期，例如關稅、通貨膨脹、利率上升、經濟衰退或經濟放緩，客戶可能因應消費者支出習慣的變化而調整存貨水準，減少本公司產品的購買，這些情況可能對本公司營收與獲利造成不利影響。
本公司業務依賴關鍵客戶，若失去或關鍵客戶的業務大幅減少，可能對本公司營收與獲利造成重大影響，並影響本公司維持或擴張業務的能力。
本公司在消費性業務上依賴數個關鍵客戶。在財務年度2025年，Walmart與Amazon.com分別佔本公司營收約29%與19%。儘管本公司與許多客戶，包括Walmart與Amazon.com，有長期的合作關係，但本公司與這些客戶並無長期供應契約，且採用個別訂單方式進行採購。若失去任何關鍵客戶或對這些客戶的銷售大幅減少，可能導致本公司營收與獲利大幅下降，並影響本公司維持或擴張業務的能力。
本公司必須持續獲得來自大型高採購量零售客戶的新訂單。未能取得預期訂單、訂單延遲或取消，或關鍵客戶施壓要求降低價格，可能會影響本公司維持或擴張業務的能力。此外，本公司可能無法持續滿足這些客戶的需求，這可能會損害客戶關係，並導致新訂單減少。
由於依賴關鍵客戶，若發生下列任何情況，本公司可能對營收與獲利造成重大不利影響：
